title: Add edge case handling: dirty worktrees, beads-sync protection, idempotency
description: Handle edge cases: skip worktrees with uncommitted changes (report error), protect the beads-sync worktree from deletion, ensure running the command twice is safe.
design:
## Context
Several edge cases need handling to make the cleanup command robust: (1) worktrees with uncommitted changes will cause `git worktree remove` to fail — report and skip, (2) the beads-sync worktree at `.git/beads-worktrees/beads-sync` must never be touched, (3) running cleanup twice must be safe (idempotent). (4) Command must handle being on a feature branch (not main) by switching to main first.

Depends on eniem-ar4 (remote branch deletion).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] If a merged worktree has uncommitted changes, `git worktree remove` failure is reported and that worktree is skipped
- [ ] The beads-sync worktree (`.git/beads-worktrees/beads-sync`) is explicitly excluded from cleanup candidates
- [ ] Running cleanup when no merged branches exist shows 'Nothing to clean up'
- [ ] Running the command twice in a row is safe (second run cleans nothing)
- [ ] Command works when currently on a feature branch (switches to main first)

## Files
- `.claude/commands/cleanup.md` (modify)

## Patterns
- Check `git worktree remove` exit code; if non-zero, report the error and continue to next worktree
- Filter candidates: only process worktrees whose path starts with `.worktrees/feat/`
- This implicitly excludes beads-sync (at `.git/beads-worktrees/`) and main worktree
- `git checkout main` at the start handles the 'currently on feature branch' case

## Tests
- Dirty worktree: skipped with error message shown to user
- beads-sync worktree: never included in cleanup candidates
- No merged branches: 'Nothing to clean up' message
- Double-run: second invocation finds nothing to clean (idempotent)
- Starting from feature branch: command switches to main before scanning

## Verify
```bash
grep -qi 'uncommitted\|dirty\|skip\|failed' .claude/commands/cleanup.md && echo pass
grep -q '.worktrees/feat/' .claude/commands/cleanup.md && echo pass
```

title: Configure beads sync-branch for worktree compatibility
design:
## Context

When using git worktrees for feature development (e.g. `.worktrees/feat/2-post-migration-config`), beads issue status changes end up duplicated:

1. **In the worktree branch** — `bd close` updates `.beads/issues.jsonl` and it gets committed with feature commits
2. **On main** — The shared SQLite DB also writes to main's `.beads/issues.jsonl`, leaving unstaged changes

This happened during spec-2 work: 8 beads were closed in the worktree, but main also had the same 8 changes as unstaged modifications. The PR carries the bead closures, so main's copy is redundant.

## Root Cause

Without `sync.branch` configured, beads commits JSONL changes directly on whatever branch you're working on. With worktrees, the shared SQLite DB updates both copies, causing duplication.

## Solution

Configure `sync.branch` so bead status changes go to a dedicated `beads-sync` branch instead of polluting feature branches:

```bash
bd config set sync.branch beads-sync
bd daemon start --auto-commit --auto-push
```

### How sync-branch works:
- Beads creates a hidden internal worktree at `.git/beads-worktrees/beads-sync/` (sparse checkout, `.beads/` only)
- All JSONL commits go to `beads-sync` branch, never to feature branches or main
- Daemon auto-pulls from remote when sync.branch is set (default)
- `beads-sync` is a permanent parallel branch — never merged into main
- SQLite DB remains the live source of truth, JSONL on sync branch is for git persistence/sharing

### Flow:
- Close bead → SQLite updates immediately
- Daemon exports → auto-commits to `beads-sync` via hidden worktree
- `--auto-push` pushes `beads-sync` to remote
- Other machines: daemon auto-pulls `beads-sync`, imports JSONL into local SQLite

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `bd config get sync.branch` returns `beads-sync`
- [ ] Daemon runs with `--auto-commit --auto-push`
- [ ] Feature branch PRs no longer contain `.beads/issues.jsonl` diffs
- [ ] Bead state syncs across worktrees without manual intervention

## Reference
- https://github.com/steveyegge/beads/blob/main/docs/WORKTREES.md

title: Create auto-tag boilerplate workflow
description: Create a new GitHub Actions workflow that automatically creates a boilerplate@x.y.z tag when quality merges into main, based on conventional commit analysis scoped to apps/boilerplate/**.
design:
## Context
This is tracer task 2 of 2. When quality merges into main, we need to automatically determine if boilerplate files changed and, if so, compute a semver bump from conventional commits and create a tag. This tag triggers the existing sync-boilerplate.yml workflow. Uses a custom shell script (not semantic-release) per spec decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New workflow `.github/workflows/auto-tag-boilerplate.yml` triggers on push to main
- [ ] Detects if `apps/boilerplate/**` files changed since last `boilerplate@*` tag
- [ ] Exits early with success if no boilerplate changes
- [ ] Analyzes conventional commits scoped to `apps/boilerplate/**` since last `boilerplate@*` tag
- [ ] Determines correct semver bump (patch for `fix:`, minor for `feat:`, major for `BREAKING CHANGE`/`feat\!:`/`fix\!:`)
- [ ] Creates and pushes `boilerplate@x.y.z` tag in correct format
- [ ] Handles first-ever tag scenario (no previous `boilerplate@*` tag) — uses all commits on main
- [ ] Fails visibly if computed tag already exists

## Files
- `.github/workflows/auto-tag-boilerplate.yml` (create) — new workflow file

## Patterns
- **Workflow structure**: Mirror `release-cli.yml` — checkout with `fetch-depth: 0`, pnpm/action-setup, setup-node
- **Permissions**: Must have `contents: write` to push tags (see `release-cli.yml` lines 10-21)
- **Finding previous tag**: `git tag -l 'boilerplate@*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1` (from `sync-boilerplate.yml` line 27)
- **Tag format**: Must be `boilerplate@x.y.z` to match `sync-boilerplate.yml` trigger on line 6
- **Commit analysis**: Use `git log $PREV_TAG..HEAD --oneline -- apps/boilerplate/` to get scoped commits
- **Semver logic**: Parse commit prefixes — `BREAKING CHANGE` or `\!:` → major, `feat:` → minor, else `fix:` → patch. Use highest bump found.
- **Version parsing**: Split `boilerplate@MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on `@` then on `.`
- **No changes case**: If `git diff --name-only $PREV_TAG..HEAD -- apps/boilerplate/` is empty, exit 0

## Tests
- Verify YAML is valid: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/auto-tag-boilerplate.yml'))"`
- Verify workflow triggers on push to main only
- Verify the script handles: no changes (skip), patch bump, minor bump, major bump, no previous tag

## Verify
```bash
python3 -c "import yaml; y=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/auto-tag-boilerplate.yml')); print('Valid YAML'); assert 'push' in y[True], 'Missing push trigger'"
```
